key_insight: Turbulent coherent structures are framed as universal thermodynamic responses to macroscopic energy throughput imbalance, captured by a computable effective order parameter (Π).
engineering_relevance: This could give engineers a principled way to identify when a flow needs finer resolution and to distinguish transient fluctuations from self-sustaining coherent structures in non-equilibrium turbulence.
method: Use renormalized Navier–Stokes equations to connect turbulence to non-equilibrium statistical physics.
Define an effective thermodynamic order parameter (Π) for coherent-structure detection.
Classify coherence by whether the flow response is a transient adjustment or an autonomous dissipative state.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical framework and claims a computable parameter for identifying necessary flow resolution, but it does not report specific datasets or numerical validation results.
watch_item: The proposal is highly conceptual, so practical adoption will depend on how Π is computed and validated across diverse turbulent flows.
paper_title: Coherence as Thermodynamic Organization: Toward a Non-Equilibrium Turbulence Theory
